summary: LunaSlip is an interactive 3D lunar landing navigator that visually evaluates how mission delays impact landing windows at the Moon's south pole. By combining verified NASA terrain data with JPL ephemerides, it allows users to simulate launch slips and instantly identify viable alternative dates based on precise Sun and Earth visibility constraints.
details:
LunaSlip turns a delayed lunar landing into an explainable search problem by combining a horizon-first visual model with synchronized date and site alternatives. Built using React 19, TypeScript, Three.js, and a Cloudflare Worker proxy, the application is driven by a framework-independent calculation engine that strictly classifies data provenance as live, cached, precomputed, or analytical to ensure scientific validity and offline reliability. The platform integrates a mission dashboard with synchronized 3D lunar context covering three verified 2-meter LROC stereo sites (Shackleton rim, Connecting Ridge, and Malapert Massif) alongside an 80-meter LOLA south-pole overview. A 360° interactive D3 horizon simulator calculates extended-disk Sun and Earth visibility against the exact local skyline, while an interactive OpenLayers GIS map utilizes NASA Moon Trek WMTS layers for spatial exploration. To handle delays, a Web Worker-powered launch-slip simulator executes configurable searches across 8,763 precomputed 2027 JPL Horizons observations, allowing mission planners to search nearby dates and regions against explicit constraints to see exactly why each candidate passes or fails. While the application functions fully offline using the bundled 2027 dataset and generated 3D meshes, querying live ephemeris data outside of this window requires an active connection to the proxy service.

Project repo: https://github.com/Tareq-Khalil/LunaSlip
